messages:
alex: FYI customer reported hallucinated tool_result mapping when making two tool calls in parallel via our API. They say outputs from tool A ended up attached to tool B.

maya: Can you paste request/response and correlation ids?

alex: Copying payload from the customer:
```json
{
  "request_id": "req_0x9f1",
  "correlation_id": "corr-5f8",
  "model": "rw-bert-1",
  "calls": [
    { "tool": "kb_search", "args": {"q": "pricing tiers"} },
    { "tool": "calc", "args": {"expr": "12*0.85"} }
  ]
}
```

alex: Response they got:
```json
{
  "request_id": "req_0x9f1",
  "results": [
    { "tool": "kb_search", "tool_result_id": "tr_1", "output": "Result about pricing..." },
    { "tool": "calc", "tool_result_id": "tr_2", "output": "\"pricing\" matched 12*0.85=10.2" }
  ],
  "tool_associations": [ {"call_index":0, "result_id":"tr_2"}, {"call_index":1, "result_id":"tr_1"} ]
}
```

maya: Yikes. That implies tool_result->call_index mapping flipped. Did they use `parallel=true` on the calls?

alex: Yes. They set `mode: parallel` in /v1/complete and saw latency spike then mismatch. Also they saw a billing surge: `usage.tokens` higher than expected.

jordan: Did they set `client_generated_ids` for each call? We rely on those to correlate in some flows.

alex: No, they didn't. They only rely on our internal generated call ids.

sre: Uploading relevant logs with correlation_id corr-5f8 and request req_0x9f1:
```text
[2026-03-10T15:02:11Z] req=req_0x9f1 corr=corr-5f8 incoming parallel fanout 2 calls
[2026-03-10T15:02:11Z] dispatched to worker w-02 (kb_search) run_id=run_88 latency_ms=120
[2026-03-10T15:02:11Z] dispatched to worker w-06 (calc) run_id=run_89 latency_ms=85
[2026-03-10T15:02:11Z] worker w-06 completed run_id=run_89 -> result_id=tr_2
[2026-03-10T15:02:11Z] worker w-02 completed run_id=run_88 -> result_id=tr_1
[2026-03-10T15:02:11Z] associator assigned result tr_2 to call_index 0 (kb_search)
[2026-03-10T15:02:11Z] associator assigned result tr_1 to call_index 1 (calc)
```

maya: Wait "associator assigned" lines indicate associator uses completion order rather than run_id mapping. That's the bug.

eng-ml: I think the associator keyed by an incrementing seq per request; when two workers finish close together there's a race and seq gets swapped. Root cause: associator iterates over pending calls but relies on completion queue without matching run_id.

alex: Repro steps I gave customer:
1) call /v1/complete with parallel true and two function calls (no client ids)
2) force calc to return faster (e.g., small expr) so results finish out-of-order
3) observe tool_associations mapping swapped

support-bot: Escalation created: INC-2026-432. Notifying @eng-runtime and @eng-sre.

maya: Temporary mitigation: advise customers to set `call_id` per call in client side. We'll push a workaround note in docs and send a targeted email.

jordan: Also instrumented a fix branch: associator will now match run_id->call_index instead of FIFO assignment. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/784

eng-sre: Deploying hotfix to staging now, will run a quick regression with the repro above and load test.

alex: Customer also reported 500 errors intermittently and 2-3s latency spikes. Any relationship?

sre: The failure correlates with a transient DB contention on associator sequences. When DB returned slow, associator fallback used in-memory queue which had the ordering bug. We'll patch both the DB timeout handling and the fallback.

maya: I'll draft the customer response: apologize, explain root cause (race in associator fallback), list workaround (set call_id), timeline for fix (hotfix in staging today, prod in ~6h), and offer to credit for the billing spike.

alex: Thanks. I'll share logs and customer consent for audit. :thumbsup:
